author: Username15737
quote: Honestly, GTA 6 is one of the biggest disappointments I've ever experienced. Between the alleged review manipulation, endless delays, and the constant exploitation of hype just to capitalize on awards season and chase GOTY recognition, this game feels more like a marketing product than a genuinely great game. It shouldn't even have been considered for GOTY in its current state. And honestly, if this game had released at the beginning of the year, around the same time as Resident Evil Requiem, it probably wouldn't be nearly as relevant anymore. The amount of hype surrounding GTA 6 is artificially keeping it in the spotlight, and without that massive marketing machine constantly pushing it, people would have moved on already. It feels like the game is relying more on its name, its release timing, and the community's obsession than on its actual quality. The performance is pretty bad, reaching 20 FPS with constant drops, accompanied by horrendous bugs, terrible collision detection, and interactions that feel completely lifeless and unresponsive. For a game of this scale, these problems are simply embarrassing. And somehow, in 2026, after 13 years of development, millions in budget, and all the resources Rockstar has at its disposal, we still don't get proper voice dubbing? Instead, we're expected to pay €80 for an unfinished, poorly optimized, unpolished, and seemingly cut-down product that absolutely does not justify its price. The story isn't necessarily terrible, which makes the whole situation even more disappointing. There is potential here, but it's buried beneath technical issues, questionable decisions, and a ridiculous amount of hype that the game simply doesn't live up to. What bothers me the most is how GTA 6 exposes the ugly side of both corporations and gaming communities. If this game had been released under a different name, without the Rockstar logo or the GTA brand behind it, people would be tearing it apart for its bugs, performance, and lack of polish. We've seen games like Cyberpunk get heavily criticized for technical problems, and even Zelda: Breath of the Wild get complaints over its 30 FPS performance. Yet when it's GTA, suddenly everything is "normal," and people defend issues they would never tolerate from any other developer. That double standard is ridiculous. Rockstar shouldn't get a free pass just because of its name, and fans shouldn't blindly defend a product simply because they have been waiting years for it. After 13 years of waiting, a massive budget, and all that hype, getting something this poorly polished for €80 is honestly a disgrace. What a waste of potential. The GTA name shouldn't be an excuse for mediocrity, and hype shouldn't replace quality. What a shame..
